answer: Linear reputation decay with lifetime caps. Each identity accrues reputation only up to a per-identity ceiling, decaying at a fixed rate; gains beyond the ceiling spill into a shared knoll pool that rivals can draw from. Sybils therefore saturate quickly, each new identity yielding diminishing returns. An attacker must fund and maintain many identities, paying full operating cost each, while only the first earns near-full weight—per-identity marginal value falls toward zero across the ocean of decoys. Costs scale linearly with identity count but returns flatten at the horizon.
